faq.q: What should I write in a food diary?
faq.a: Start with three essentials: what you ate, roughly how much, and when. Once that feels easy, add how hungry you were on a scale of 1 to 10 and one word for how you felt. Calories and macros are optional; an app can work them out for you.

faq.q: How long should I keep a food diary?
faq.a: Give it at least one full week to build the habit, then two to four weeks to see patterns. Many people keep going for months because it becomes quick and useful, but even a short diary can show you a lot about your eating.

faq.q: Do I have to count calories in a food diary?
faq.a: No. A food diary can be as simple as what, when and how you felt. Calories are useful for some goals, but plenty of people get most of the benefit from noticing patterns alone. Fimbl's Calm mode (Premium) even replaces calorie numbers with gentle grades.

faq.q: Is a food diary app better than paper?
faq.a: Neither is better in general. Paper is flexible and has no setup. An app is faster thanks to search, barcode scanning and saved meals, sends reminders and shows trends for you. The best choice is the one you'll keep opening.

faq.q: What if I forget to log a meal?
faq.a: Log what you remember, or simply carry on from the next meal. A missed meal or day doesn't ruin a diary; trying to start over from scratch is what usually ends it. A helpful rule is: miss a day if you have to, but try not to miss two.

faq.q: Does keeping a food diary help with weight loss?
faq.a: Research consistently links food logging with better weight-loss results, especially logging often and consistently. In a trial of nearly 1,700 adults, the number of food records kept was among the strongest predictors of weight lost. The evidence shows a strong association rather than proof for every individual.
